summary: Answered Shawn's question - can the reasoning strategies be template-driven declarative design, the same as the agent-scaffold system - with a real, verified prototype rather than an opinion. Built a ReasoningStrategySpec schema and render_strategy.py generator as a sibling system to DECLARATIVE-GENERATIVE-AGENT-TEMPLATE.md (deliberately separate, since the file convention differs). Proved it via round-trip on 2 of 35 strategies: the generator reproduces the real files exactly except for one intentionally-dropped one-time migration line and cosmetic line-wrap width. A wrong assumption (steps_description being universal boilerplate) was caught by the round-trip diff itself and fixed before this trail claimed success.
earned_constraints: a round-trip proof (generate, then diff against the real artifact) catches assumptions that structural inspection alone misses - the steps_description field would have shipped wrong if this trail had stopped at 'the six sections look the same across both files' instead of actually generating and diffing

when extending a 'declare once, generate projections' pattern to a new file convention, keep it a separate small system rather than branching an existing generator on incompatible shapes - this trail deliberately did not touch scaffold.py
next_seed: If Shawn wants to continue: (1) verify the laws/permissions invariant against all 34 non-selector strategy files, not just the 2 read so far, (2) write specs for the remaining 32 via the same reverse-engineer-then-diff discipline, (3) then decide whether to actually regenerate the real files or keep specs as a parallel source, and separately decide whether selector.md's derivable Families list is worth generating.
